title: File.join recurses on a self-referencing array until the C stack is exhausted
live_proof: upstream fixed it in 1737589f0 (1737589f004d6b6409e8d4222ed5064af03ca802) (2026-09-08), which is in master and postdates the 4.0.0-rc2 pin (2026-03-12); the pin's tree has no such fix. Host ASan at the pin: stack-overflow (with MRB_HEAP_PAGE_SIZE=1: stack-overflow); the same case on master: no report
fidelity: the trigger is the Ruby test upstream added with its fix, extracted onto a self-contained harness that collects failures instead of aborting, so one script yields one verdict. It is upstream's own reproduction, not a reduction of ours; what it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it

sysalloc-none.oracle: the watchdog killed it at 25 s (it does not terminate)

sysalloc-bounds.oracle: the watchdog killed it at 25 s (it does not terminate)

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: the guest timeout killed it at 25 s (it does not terminate)

status: sysalloc-none, sysalloc-bounds and sublet-gc measured 2026-10-06 on the Capstone application VM; cheribsd-revocation measured 2026-10-06 on CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation at its default
